Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 29 s. 2023 APR 27 2023 HON. ROLLY M. QUEBRAL Mayor Municipality of Maconacon Province of Isabela Dear Mayor Quebral: This has reference to your letter dated October II, 2022 wherein you raised issues regarding the accreditation of Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) for purposes of representation to the Local Special Bodies (LSBs). For ease of reference, we quote the queries proffered: If no CSOs were able to be accredited in the prescribed accreditation period of 60 days, does it imply automatically that no more CSOs are allowed to make representation to the Local Special Bodies? 2. Can we use the previously accredited CSOs in the Executive Order ofthe Local Chief Executive? 3. Beyond the 60-day period of accreditation, can the Sanggunian still accredit CSOs for representation in the LSBs? On the First Issue: Foremost, we deem it proper to emphasize that no less than the 1987 Constitution institutionalizes the role of NGOs and CSOs in governance at all levels of social, political, and economic decision-making. One of the State policies found in Article II, Section 23 of the 1987 provides that "The State shall encourage non-govemmental, community-based, or sectoral organizations that promote the welfare of the nation". Consistent with the aforecited constitutional provision, Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, provides for the legal and institutional framework for expanded participation of civil society in local governance especially in promoting local accountability and answerability. More specifically, it allocates to non-governmental organizations (NGOs) and people's organizations (POs) specific seats in local special bodies (LSBs). These special bodies include the Local Development Council, the Local Health Board, and the Local School Board. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

It should be noted that the representation of NGOs in the LSBs shall be subject to the accreditation of the sanggunian concerned subject to the criteria provided by law. Article 64 (c) and (d) of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 7160 (hereinafter the "IRR") states: "Section 64. Procedure and Guidelines for the Selection of Representatives of People's Organizations, Nongovernmental Organization, or the Private Sector in Local Special Bodies. (c) Completion of the accreditation process. - The Sanggunian shall complete the accreditation process within sixtv (60) days from the promulqation of these Rules or within the same period from the organization of newly-elected sanggunian. (d) Within fifteen (15 days) after the accreditation process, the DILG field officer assigned in the LGU shall call all accredited people's organizations, NGOs, or the private sector to a meeting where these organizations shall choose from among themselves which people's organizations, NGOs or private sector will be represented in the local special bodies. " The above provisions are echoed in DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2022-0831, issued on July 15, 2022. Item 3.14 states that: "1.4. Accreditation — refers to the process of granting authorization, within 60 days from the orqanization of the newly elected sanggunian. to an organization for purposes of representation to a local special body. An organization may still be accredited after the prescribed 60-day period for other purposes, such as participation in local govemment programs." (Emphasis Supplied) As aforequoted, the rules provide that the sanggunian shall complete the accreditation process of POs, NGOs, or the private sector within sixty (60) days from the promulgation of said rules or within the same period from the organization of the newly-elected Sanggunian, and within fifteen (15) days after the accreditation process. The DILG Field Officer assigned in the LGU shall call all POs, NGOs, or private sector to a meeting where these organizations shall choose from among themselves which organizations will be presented in the local special bodies. Hence, before the LSB can function and conduct official business, the determination of CSO representatives must first be ascertained. However, we do not lose sight of the possibility where no NGO, PO or private orqanization was accredited within the period of 60 either because of non-availability. of these organizations within the LGU concerned at the time the call for accreditation was issued or because no NGO or CSO met all the requirements for accreditation2 I Guidelines on the Accreditation of Civil Society Organizations and Selection of Representatives to the Local Special Bodies 2 4.23, DILG Memorandum Circular 2022-83. Page 2 of 5

Accordingly, in the foregoing circumstances, we opine that although the rules prescribe for the organization of local development councils within a 60-day period, the sanqqunian may still carry out its accreditation process even beyond the qoverninq period for accreditation to allow CSOs to make representation to the Local Special Bodies It bears to note that while a period to complete the accreditation process was provided by the IRR, yet a careful reading of the provision yields that it contemplates a situation where the process of accreditation has already commenced upon submission of application of organizations seeking for new accreditation or renewal in compliance to the call for accreditation under Item 4.2 of DILG MC 2022-833. To our mind, this is the clear import of the use of the words "shall complete" in the rule. Further, we submit that a liberal application of the rule in favor of ensuring citizen participation in local governance and development processes is needed in the herein instance. It is only this kind of interpretation that can give meaning and substance to the principle of participatory governance as envisioned by the Constitution and the Local Government Code of 19914, The Supreme Court in Ursua vs Court of Appeals5 elucidation on the principle that the intent or the spirit of the law is the law itself also finds application in the herein legal query, to wit: "Well settled is that statutes are to be construed in the light of the purposes to be achieved and the evils sought to be remedied. We, therefore, have to consider the spirit and reason of the statute where a literal meaning would lead to absurdity, contradiction, injustice, or would defeat the clear purpose of the lawmakers These further exists a valid presumption that undesirable consequences were never intended by a legislative measure and that a construction of which the statute is fairly susceptible is favored to avoid all objectionable, mischievous, indefensible, wrongful, evil and injurious consequences. Inevitably, if we are to stick to the strict and literal reading of Section 64 (c) which restricts the sanggunian to complete the accreditation within 60 days from its organization, there may be some local government units without NGO or CSO representation in their LSBs denying them the representation that those who drafted the Constitution intended them to have undermining the Constitutional intent quoted above. On the Second Issue: For your guidance, may we direct your attention Article 64 (a) of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act 7160 which provides and we quote: "ARTICLE 64. Procedures and Guidelines for Selection of Representatives of People's Organizations, Nongovernmental Organizations, or the Private Sector in Local Special Bodies. 4 Section 3. Operative Principles Of Decentralization, Republic Act No. 7160. (I) The participation of the private sector in local governance, particularly in the delivery of basic services, shall be encouraged to ensure the viability of local autonomy as an alternative strategy for sustainable development; 5 G.R. No. 202242, July 17, 2012 Page 3 of 5

(a) Call for application — Within thirty (30) days from the approval of these Rules and thereafter, within thirty (30) days from the organization of the newly elected sanggunian, each sanggunian concerned shall call a!] community-based people's organizations or NGOs. including business and professional groups. and other similar aggrupations to apply with the LGU concemed for accreditation for membership in the local special bodies. The application shall include a duly approved board resolution of the people's organizations, 32 NGOs or the private sector concerned, certificate of registration, list of officers, accomplishments, and financial data of the organization. [Emphasis Supplied]" Moreover, quoted hereunder are the relevant provisions of DILG Memorandum Circular 2022-83, viz: "4.2 Call for Accreditation. 4.2. I. Within the 1st week of August, the sanggunian, in coordination with the CSO Desk Officer, Local PDO or a duly designated LGU appointive official, shall issue a Notice of Call for Accreditation (Annex A) and send an invitation (Annex B) to all CSOs listed in the final updated Directory of CSOs, whether previouslv accredited or seeking accreditation for the first time. " [Emphasis Supplied] Based on the foregoing, all NGOs, CSOs, POs, and other similar groups, seeking to sit in LSBs, whether previously accredited or seeking accreditation for the first time, shall go through the process of accreditation which takes place at the start of the three-year term of local officials. Any previously accredited organization is to renew accreditation for the purpose of representation in a local special body. On the Third Issue With regard to the last issue, may we direct your attention to relevant provisions of DILG Memorandum Circular 2022-083 which discusses the legal consequence of not applying for accreditation within the sixty-day (60) day period. 1.0 Background xxx 1.4. The accreditation of CSOs is a continuous process wherein a CSO may apply and obtain accreditation at any time. The only legal effect of not applying for accreditation within the sixty-day (60) day period prescribed by law and reiterated in this Memorandum Circular is that such organization is not entitled for a representation in a local special body. xxx Page 4 of 5

3.0 Definition of Terms xxx 3.12. Accreditation — refers to the process of granting authorization, within 60 days from the organization of the newly elected Sanggunian, to an organization for purposes of representation to a local special body. An organizatiorp may still be accredited after the prescribed 60-day period for other purposes, such as participation in local government programs. xxx Based on the foregoing provisions, the Sanggunian may still accredit CSOs beyond the 60-day period of accreditation. However, subsequently accredited organizations may not be represented in Local Special Bodies, but are allowed to participate in the implementation of programs of the concerned local government unit. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope the foregoing sufficiently clarified your queries. Thank you very much. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SE ETARY N TOR R. LLAMAS er ecret ryfor External, Legal and Legislative Affairs LL RPB/LRALLD0vpr Copy furnished DIR.
